gen-gf-akaya-telivigala-fs-rowan: Akaya Telivigala crowds its letters like beads pressed on a wire, each round c pulled open. But Rowan, a text serif with generous curves, is better kept away from long, dense paragraphs.
gen-gf-amita-fs-neco: Relaxed and friendly, Amita looks traced with a single marker, every letter rounded and open. Neco brings a measured swell from hairline to stem, dignified enough to carry a brief stretch of text.
gen-gf-amita-fs-plein: Amita feels like one marker traced every letter, soft and rounded, with no pressure swell where a curve turns. Plein, the sans-serif body, opens a clear channel into each round letter.
gen-gf-amita-fs-recia: Amita looks like a bent paperclip, soft and friendly, with no shifts in stroke weight across its rounded letters. Recia, a serif with sturdy hairlines, suits modest helpings of text.
gen-gf-architects-daughter-fs-neco: Unshaded handwriting with wide-swinging s curves: that's Architects Daughter. Neco's thin strokes are clearly lighter yet never fragile, and that gap between loose line and measured serif is the pair's whole appeal.
gen-gf-architects-daughter-fs-recia: Loose pencil-like lines, and a g that never changes weight. Architects Daughter is best at graceful, relaxed ease, while Recia, a serif drawn with a barely tilted nib, does sharp, authoritative reading.
gen-gf-architects-daughter-fs-spline-san: Relaxed hand-drawn warmth, with s curves that open wide and diagonals matching the stems. And Spline Sans, contemporary and approachable with wide gaps, is happier with quick snippets than with pages of text.
gen-gf-architects-daughter-plus-jakarta-: Monoline and precise, the body text keeps its curve endings well apart. Plus Jakarta Sans sits under Architects Daughter's relaxed handwriting, though it is not built for lengthy paragraphs.
gen-gf-architects-daughter-sora: Sora draws its curves with no pressure swell, keeping c and s widely parted. Sora holds a precise geometry that gives Architects Daughter's graceful, relaxed hand an exact partner in quick lines.
gen-gf-astloch-fs-paquito: Tightly knit, rope-fiber letters that crowd up toward the cap line. Paquito, a serif whose lowercase nearly meets the capitals, stays approachable while Astloch does the bold shouting, and neither is for lengthy paragraphs.
